overview: Two different qualities of a measurement — one is about being close to the true value, the other about being consistent.
genZNote: Accuracy: hitting the bullseye. Precision: hitting the same spot every time, bullseye or not.

aspects.label: Definition
aspects.valueA: How close a measured value is to the true or accepted value.
aspects.valueB: How close repeated measurements are to each other, regardless of the true value.

aspects.label: Can You Have One Without the Other?
aspects.valueA: Yes — you can be accurate on average but inconsistent (low precision).
aspects.valueB: Yes — you can be very precise but consistently wrong (systematic error, low accuracy).

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: A scale that reads 50.0g, 50.1g, 49.9g for a known 50g weight — accurate.
aspects.valueB: A scale that reads 52.0g, 52.1g, 52.0g for a known 50g weight — precise but not accurate.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: A classic viva question uses a dartboard analogy: accurate-and-precise hits the bullseye tightly; precise-but-not-accurate clusters tightly off-centre.
overlay.commonMisconception: High precision does not guarantee high accuracy — a consistently miscalibrated instrument gives precise but inaccurate readings.
